list.title: SLA policies
list.intro: Response and resolution targets per plan and priority in business minutes, the business hours they count in, and what happens when a clock runs out. The worker applies them every minute from real timestamps.

new.title: New SLA policy
new.intro: Targets, business hours and escalation for one or more plans. Values are prefilled with the seeded defaults.

edit.title: Edit SLA policy
edit.intro: Changes apply to new tickets and to clocks that are still running; stopped clocks keep their result.

howItWorks.title: What the worker does with these policies
howItWorks.clocks: Every ticket gets the policy of its organisation's plan (or the default) when it is created; the first-response clock stops with the first agent reply, the resolution clock when the ticket is solved. "Pending" pauses both.
howItWorks.warnings: When the remaining business time drops to the warning share of the target, the assignee gets an in-app event and an e-mail — once per clock, never for a paused ticket.
howItWorks.breaches: Past the due date the ticket is flagged as breached; the assignee, the named recipients and — if enabled — every platform admin are e-mailed.
howItWorks.autoClose: Solved tickets close themselves after the configured number of days (empty = never). Tickets without a policy of their own follow the default policy here.
howItWorks.selection: One policy per plan; plans without a policy use the default. The job runs every minute (support-sla) and evaluates up to 2 000 tickets per run.

empty.title: No SLA policy yet
empty.text: Without a policy tickets show "no SLA policy" and the worker neither warns nor escalates. Create one and mark it as the default.

general.title: Policy
general.text: Name, the plans it applies to, and whether it is the default for every plan without a policy of its own.

form.name: Name
form.nameHint: Shown in the ticket list and on the ticket; at most 80 characters.
form.plansHint: A plan can belong to one policy only. Leave every plan unchecked for a policy that applies through the default flag alone.
form.isDefaultHint: Applies to every plan without an explicit policy and decides the auto-close of tickets without a policy. Exactly one policy is the default; to replace it, mark another one.

targets.title: Targets
targets.text: Business minutes from the ticket's creation (or reopening) to the first agent reply and to the resolution. Whole minutes; a day counts as 24 hours of business time.
targets.caption: Targets per priority for first response and resolution
targets.hint: Between 5 minutes and 90 days; the first-response target cannot exceed the resolution target.

hours.title: Business hours
hours.text: The clocks count only inside these windows, in the zone below. Weekends and evenings do not count.
hours.timezoneHint: IANA name, for example Europe/Berlin. The zone also formats the due times in notifications.
hours.hint: One window per day (a lunch break needs the API). No enabled day means the clocks run around the clock, seven days a week.

escalation.title: Escalation
escalation.text: Who hears about a clock that is running out or has run out, and when solved tickets close themselves.
escalation.warningPercentHint: 1–99. At 80 % the assignee is warned when a fifth of the target is left.
escalation.escalateToAdmins: Escalate breaches to every platform admin
escalation.escalateToAdminsHint: On a breach every account with the PLATFORM_ADMIN role is e-mailed next to the assignee and the named recipients.
escalation.notifyUserIdsHint: Platform operators only; customers can never be named here.
escalation.autoCloseDaysHint: Whole days after the resolution; empty or 0 = never. Tickets without a policy follow the default policy's value.

form.createdTitle: Policy created. New tickets of its plans pick it up at once.

actions.setDefaultText: The current default loses the flag. Plans without their own policy and the auto-close of tickets without a policy follow the new default from now on; existing tickets keep their policy.
actions.deleteText: The policy is removed for good. Its plans fall back to the default policy for new tickets.
actions.deleteBlockedInUse: {count, plural, one {# ticket references this policy} other {# tickets reference this policy}}; it cannot be deleted. Reassign or close those tickets first, or keep the policy.

errors.forbidden: This action needs the platform admin role with two-factor authentication.
errors.not_found: That policy does not exist (any more).
errors.unchanged: Nothing to change — the policy already looks like this.
errors.in_use: {count, plural, one {# ticket references} other {# tickets reference}} this policy; it cannot be deleted.
errors.is_default: The default policy cannot be deleted. Make another policy the default first.
errors.default_required: The default flag cannot be switched off. Mark another policy as the default instead.
errors.plan_taken: One of the selected plans already belongs to another policy.
errors.generic: That did not work. Please try again.

fieldErrors.order: Must not be shorter than the first-response target.
fieldErrors.window: The end must be after the start.
fieldErrors.timezone: Unknown time zone. Use an IANA name such as Europe/Berlin.
fieldErrors.not_found: One of the recipients is no platform operator.
fieldErrors.default_required: Mark another policy as the default instead.

notices.updated: Policy saved. Running clocks of its tickets follow the new targets at the next change; the worker applies the new warning share within a minute.
